title: Initials that fit
hints: The output needs one byte per initial **plus one for `'\0'`**. So with `cap` bytes you can store at most `cap - 1` initials. And with `cap == 0` you can't even store the terminator.

Walk `name` with a flag that says "the next letter starts a word" (true at the start and after a space). Keep an output index `n`. Before writing an initial, check `n + 1 < cap`; if not, return false.

`if (cap == 0) return false; size_t n = 0; bool start = true; for (...) { if (s[i] == ' ') { start = true; } else if (start) { if (n + 1 >= cap) return false; out[n++] = (char)toupper((unsigned char)s[i]); start = false; } } out[n] = '\0'; return true;`
